#### 1. Bruck syndrome 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.731)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:18169)

**Proposed mechanism:** FKBP10 (HGNC:18169) —DISRUPTS→ Collagen folding and cross-linking (GO:0006457); Collagen folding and cross-linking (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Osteogenesis imperfecta (HP:0002659); Collagen folding and cross-linking (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0005604); FKBP10 (HGNC:18169) —LEADS_TO→ Contractures of fingers and toes (HP:0002706); FKBP10 (HGNC:18169) —LEADS_TO→ Micrognathia (HP:0000347). Loss-of-function mutations in FKBP10 disrupt collagen folding and cross-linking, a shared pathway implicated in the skeletal abnormalities seen in MONDO:0012592 and the contractures and micrognathia characteristic of Bruck syndrome 1 (MONDO:0009806).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in FKBP10 in individuals with MONDO:0012592 or Bruck syndrome 1 that do not segregate with the phenotype, or demonstration that FKBP10 is not essential for collagen processing in relevant cell types, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs113896308 (a known pathogenic variant in FKBP10))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of FKBP10 in collagen processing offers a potential therapeutic target for both MONDO:0012592 and Bruck syndrome 1, aiming to restore collagen integrity and ameliorate skeletal and connective tissue defects.
